organisingLogic: US-China strategic competition is the master condition; each condition below describes how that contest, or a connected global force, can transmit into Taiwan and then STE.

conditions.name: US-China strategic competition
conditions.currentAssessment: Strategic competition remains the master condition for Taiwan risk. Military, technology, trade, investment and diplomatic competition are increasingly connected, making Taiwan a central point at which wider rivalry can transmit into business operations.
conditions.taiwanTransmission: A deterioration in the relationship can increase pressure on Taiwan without immediately becoming a military conflict.
watchIndicators: New US or China restrictions linked to Taiwan
Changes in deterrence or alliance commitments
Direct disruption of cross-border business or financial channels

conditions.name: China political trajectory and Taiwan objective
conditions.currentAssessment: China's Taiwan objective remains connected to national identity, political legitimacy, military modernisation and national rejuvenation. Domestic economic or political pressure may increase the use of controlled external pressure without implying an immediate decision for war.
conditions.taiwanTransmission: The most likely near-term transmission is calibrated political, administrative, economic or information pressure.
watchIndicators: Changes in official Taiwan red-line language
Economic or regulatory action against Taiwan-linked companies
Civil-military mobilisation or resilience preparation

conditions.name: Taiwan Strait military and maritime pressure
conditions.currentAssessment: Military exercises, air activity, maritime pressure and coast guard operations form an elevated baseline. The important change is not any single exercise but whether the pattern becomes more frequent, prolonged, geographically restrictive or disruptive to commercial activity.
conditions.taiwanTransmission: Pressure can affect staff confidence, shipping, insurance, supplier lead times and customer decisions before a formal blockade.
watchIndicators: Exercises that effectively surround Taiwan
Restrictions on commercial air or sea routes
Boarding, interception or communications incidents
Use of civilian transport or logistics assets

conditions.name: US political, alliance and Taiwan policy trajectory
conditions.currentAssessment: US policy toward China and Taiwan is shaped by the presidency, Congress, defence planning, alliance commitments and domestic political competition. A more explicit US commitment may strengthen deterrence while also increasing China's perception that Taiwan is aligning with the United States.
conditions.taiwanTransmission: Policy changes can alter deterrence, sanctions exposure, technology access and the likelihood of allied responses to disruption.
watchIndicators: Taiwan-related legislation or security commitments
Changes in alliance posture
Political pressure to restrict China-linked technology or suppliers
Divergence between US and allied implementation

conditions.name: US Federal Reserve policy and global borrowing costs
conditions.currentAssessment: US Federal Reserve decisions transmit through global funding costs, exchange rates, credit conditions and investor risk appetite. The Taiwan question is therefore affected not only by war or sanctions but also by the cost and availability of financing throughout the world.
conditions.taiwanTransmission: Higher-for-longer US rates can increase financing costs, strengthen the US dollar, pressure TWD, raise supplier and customer credit risk, and reduce the financial flexibility available during a Taiwan disruption.
watchIndicators: Fed rate decisions and forward guidance
US dollar and TWD movement
Credit-spread and project-financing changes
Customer payment or supplier liquidity deterioration
Any restriction affecting NRA cash sweeps or repatriation
relatedCfoQuestions: Are we out of pocket cash wise?

conditions.name: US-China technology and AI confrontation
conditions.currentAssessment: The technology contest covers semiconductors, AI, data, cloud infrastructure, sensors, industrial software, communications and dual-use systems. Taiwan is central to this ecosystem, while STE systems increasingly depend on trusted technology and resilient electronics supply chains.
conditions.taiwanTransmission: Technology restrictions can create supplier eligibility, licensing, component availability, cost and delivery problems without a military escalation.
watchIndicators: Controls on AI chips, memory, sensors or advanced manufacturing
Trusted-origin requirements
Restrictions on Chinese or Taiwan-linked suppliers
Customer restrictions on AI, cloud or communications architecture

conditions.name: Sanctions, export controls and selective economic pressure
conditions.currentAssessment: Economic pressure is likely to remain a usable instrument for both Washington and Beijing because it can signal resolve without immediately causing full economic rupture. Ambiguous restrictions can be operationally difficult because companies must interpret them while continuing delivery.
conditions.taiwanTransmission: Customs delays, licensing, sanctions, shipping restrictions or pressure on cross-border companies can affect Taiwan projects, suppliers, insurance and banking.
watchIndicators: Sanctions involving Taiwan, China or strategic industries
Restrictions on rail, electronics, power or communications components
Customs or licensing delays
Banking restrictions involving Taiwan transactions

conditions.name: Taiwan domestic, economic and financial resilience
conditions.currentAssessment: Taiwan remains economically capable and institutionally functioning, but its global technology concentration and exposure to cross-Strait disruption create vulnerabilities. Domestic political contestation matters when it affects infrastructure decisions, emergency response, regulation, energy, investment or customer budgets.
conditions.taiwanTransmission: Financial stress may appear through TWD volatility, delayed payments, higher insurance, supplier liquidity pressure or restrictions on moving cash before physical disruption occurs.
watchIndicators: Material TWD volatility
Customer payment delays
Supplier liquidity deterioration
Changes to foreign investment or critical infrastructure policy
Energy or infrastructure reliability concerns

conditions.name: Middle East and Russia-Ukraine conflicts affecting the Taiwan calculation
conditions.currentAssessment: The Middle East and Russia-Ukraine conflicts matter to Taiwan when they alter US military attention, energy and shipping costs, sanctions precedent, alliance cohesion, defence-industrial capacity or China's assessment of Western willingness to absorb economic costs.
conditions.taiwanTransmission: A crisis elsewhere can change deterrence, increase energy and freight costs, divert resources or provide China with lessons about sanctions and coalition response.
watchIndicators: US force diversion from the Indo-Pacific
Sanctions precedents applied to China
Shipping or energy disruption
Chinese diplomatic or economic support for Russia or Middle Eastern actors
Military lessons transferred to the Taiwan scenario

conditions.name: Taiwan whole-of-society and infrastructure resilience
conditions.currentAssessment: Taiwan's resilience depends on power, telecommunications, ports, transport, cyber systems, public communications, emergency supplies and staff continuity. Natural hazards and cyber incidents matter even when they are not caused by geopolitical conflict, because a contested environment can make recovery slower and attribution more difficult.
conditions.taiwanTransmission: A limited disruption can create project delay, staff-safety exposure or supplier failure while the wider political situation remains below the threshold of war.
watchIndicators: Damage to cables, ports, power or transport systems
Cyber incidents affecting government, rail or infrastructure operators
Emergency-response and continuity exercises
Typhoons or earthquakes near operating sites
Changes to evacuation or shelter guidance
